title: Ordinary tensor-generator interchange on strict quotient systems
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite coefficient extensions $E\subset L\subset M$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, allowing equality, with valuation rings, chosen uniformizers and quotient rings $A_{F,n}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes have $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use their small pro-etale ringed sequence sites and categories $\mathscr S_F(X)$ of module sheaves, equivalently strict quotient-module systems with the actual semilinear quotient transitions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Write $u_{f,F}$ for ordinary inverse image and $s_{L/E,X}$ for ordinary scalar extension on these module categories. Use exactly the ordinary adjunction-mate compositor $c^F_{h,k}:u_{kh,F}\cong u_{h,F}u_{k,F}$, tensor comparison $\kappa_f:s_{L/E,X}u_{f,E}\cong u_{f,L}s_{L/E,Y}$, scalar associator $\alpha_X:s_{M/L,X}s_{L/E,X}\cong s_{M/E,X}$ and multiplication unitor $e_X:s_{E/E,X}\cong1$ specified in [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. Composition is written from right to left.

For $Z\xrightarrow hW\xrightarrow kV$ and every $N\in\mathscr S_E(V)$,
$$u_{h,L}(\kappa_{k,N})\circ\kappa_{h,u_{k,E}N}\circ s_{L/E,Z}(c^E_{h,k,N})=c^L_{h,k,s_{L/E,V}N}\circ\kappa_{kh,N}.$$
For every $f:X\to Y$,
$$u_{f,E}(e_Y)\circ\kappa_f^{E/E}=e_Xu_{f,E},$$
$$u_{f,M}(\alpha_Y)\circ\kappa_f^{M/L}s_{L/E,Y}\circ s_{M/L,X}(\kappa_f^{L/E})=\kappa_f^{M/E}\circ\alpha_Xu_{f,E}.$$
These are equalities of natural transformations of ordinary whole-system functors. They commute with every vertical site restriction and horizontal quotient transition and, upon degreewise application, are equal cochain maps of arbitrary unbounded complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Their values on the iterated adjunction-unit and tensor generators are respectively $\gamma_h\gamma_k(1\otimes x)$, $\gamma_f(x)$ on $1\otimes\gamma_f(x)$, and $\gamma_f(cb\otimes x)$ on $c\otimes(b\otimes\gamma_f(x))$. Equality is determined through the inverse-image and tensor adjunctions on all local sections; it does not require arbitrary sheaf sections to be globally pure tensors. No flatness of the quotient coefficient maps is assumed. This statement concerns ordinary systems and cochain maps only, without derived scalar functors or realization.

proof.text: Work on the ringed sequence sites, not separately in derived fibers [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Let $R_{f,F}$ be the specified ordinary right adjoint of $u_{f,F}$ and let $\sigma_{L/E}(y)=1\otimes y$ be the scalar-extension unit. The tensor adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus] and the inverse-image adjunction of [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems], composed as in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], give an injective equality test: two maps out of $s_{L/E,X}u_{f,E}N$ agree if their composites with $x\mapsto1\otimes\gamma_f(x)$ agree for every section $x$ of $N$ at every sequence-site object. Indeed their successive transposes are maps out of $N$, and the displayed composites are precisely their values on sections. For $s_{M/L,X}s_{L/E,X}u_{f,E}N$ the same test uses $x\mapsto1\otimes(1\otimes\gamma_f(x))$. Scalar extension is the sheafified sectionwise tensor: linear maps out of it are determined before sheafification by the images of $b\otimes y$, and $b\otimes y=b(1\otimes y)$; uniqueness in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] then gives equality of sheaf maps. These tests apply to the whole sequence-site adjunctions. They require neither flatness nor a representation of arbitrary sheaf sections by global pure tensors. In Lean, the normalized ordinary scalar adjunction is obtained from [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction], applied to the recorded scalar model with its object and map equations. Composing this adjunction once or twice with inverse image gives exactly the two sectionwise equality tests. Private proved helpers give scalar linearity and naturality of these unit tensors.

proof.text: Normalize the geometric compositor by its mate, rather than choosing a tensor isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with $L_1=u_{kh,F}$, $L_2=u_{h,F}u_{k,F}$, $R_1=R_{kh,F}$, $R_2=R_{k,F}R_{h,F}$ and $\delta:R_2\cong R_1$ the specified direct-image fiber-product-pasting isomorphism of [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. The composite unit is the pasted pair of units by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Consequently, after the canonical pasting identification of the test objects, $c^F_{h,k}(\gamma_{kh}(x))=\gamma_h(\gamma_k(x))$. This is the unit equation in the cited mate lemma, so it holds for the prescribed $c^F$. Naturality of the same unit gives $u_{f,F}(a)(\gamma_f(x))=\gamma_f(a(x))$ for every module-system morphism $a$. Both equations are equations of sections of whole-system maps, retaining the pasting identification; no equality of the un-identified base-change functors is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints, unit characterization; Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits, composite adjunction. Applied to the prescribed pasting mate.

proof.text:
For the first equation use Step 1 with $f=kh$. On $1\otimes\gamma_{kh}(x)$, Step 2 followed by the defining scalar/pullback formula in [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems] gives for the left route
$$1\otimes\gamma_{kh}(x)\longmapsto1\otimes\gamma_h(\gamma_k(x))\longmapsto\gamma_h(1\otimes\gamma_k(x))\longmapsto\gamma_h(\gamma_k(1\otimes x)).$$
The last arrow uses naturality of $\gamma_h$ for $\kappa_k$. The right route sends the same generator first to $\gamma_{kh}(1\otimes x)$ and then, by Step 2 over $L$, to $\gamma_h(\gamma_k(1\otimes x))$. The two transposes therefore agree on every source section, and injectivity of the adjunction test proves the first equality. This also establishes exactly its asserted generator value.

proof.text: For the scalar-unit equation take $L=E$ and apply the same equality test. The route through $\kappa_f^{E/E}$ sends $1\otimes\gamma_f(x)$ to $\gamma_f(1\otimes x)$; applying $u_{f,E}(e_Y)$ gives $\gamma_f(x)$ by naturality of the unit and the formula $e_Y(1\otimes x)=x$. The route through $e_Xu_{f,E}$ also gives $\gamma_f(x)$. These are the multiplication unitor and scalar/pullback map specified in [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. Step 1 proves equality on the entire source object; the argument includes arbitrary source sections $x$ and uses no cancellation of a coefficient.

source.place: lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product. Agent calculation with the prescribed whole-sequence comparison maps.

proof.text:
For the scalar-tower equation test first on $1\otimes(1\otimes\gamma_f(x))$ using the twice-composed adjunction of Step 1. The three arrows on the left give successively $1\otimes\gamma_f(1\otimes x)$, $\gamma_f(1\otimes(1\otimes x))$, and $\gamma_f(1\otimes x)$. The two arrows on the right give $1\otimes\gamma_f(x)$ and $\gamma_f(1\otimes x)$. Here the associator multiplies the two coefficient factors, and the last left arrow uses naturality of $\gamma_f$ for $\alpha_Y$, all with the formulas of [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. This proves the equality. To spell out its coefficient formula, take coefficient sections $b,c$ on the original test object and use their images on the pulled-back object. On $c\otimes(b\otimes\gamma_f(x))$ the left route is
$$c\otimes\gamma_f(b\otimes x)\longmapsto\gamma_f(c\otimes(b\otimes x))\longmapsto\gamma_f(cj(b)\otimes x),$$
and the right route is $cj(b)\otimes\gamma_f(x)\mapsto\gamma_f(cj(b)\otimes x)$. The inclusions suppress $j$ in the statement's notation $cb$. Coefficients written inside $\gamma_f$ are on that source test object; the full map equality for all target-local coefficients already follows from the adjunction test and linearity, without trying to push arbitrary target sections back to the source.

source.place: lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product. Agent calculation with the prescribed whole-sequence comparison maps.

proof.text: Check vertical restrictions explicitly. For a site arrow $r$ at a fixed quotient index, the maps in [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems] are module-sheaf maps: $r(\gamma_f(x))=\gamma_f(r(x))$ under base change and $r(b\otimes y)=r(b)\otimes r(y)$. Thus restricting the three common values in Steps 3--5 gives, respectively, $\gamma_h\gamma_k(1\otimes r(x))$, $\gamma_f(r(x))$, and $\gamma_f(r(c)j(r(b))\otimes r(x))$. These are also the values obtained by first restricting all inputs: $r(1)=1$ and $r(cj(b))=r(c)j(r(b))$ because the coefficient maps are maps of ring sheaves. The geometric pasting identification commutes with $r$ by naturality of the specified direct-image pasting map. The equality test of Step 1 therefore gives every vertical restriction square.

source.place: lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product. Agent calculation with the prescribed whole-sequence comparison maps.

proof.text:
Check horizontal transitions without tensor exactness. Write $q^F_{m,n}:A_{F,m}\to A_{F,n}$ for an actual quotient transition, and $t$ for a system's corresponding semilinear section map. On scalar generators the transition is $b\otimes y\mapsto q^L_{m,n}(b)\otimes t(y)$; on iterated scalar generators it sends $c\otimes(b\otimes y)$ to $q^M_{m,n}(c)\otimes(q^L_{m,n}(b)\otimes t(y))$. The whole-system unit commutes with transitions, $t(\gamma_f(x))=\gamma_f(t(x))$, by [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. Since the scalar coefficient maps form maps of quotient diagrams,
$$q^M_{m,n}(cj(b))=q^M_{m,n}(c)j(q^L_{m,n}(b)),\qquad q^F_{m,n}(1)=1.$$
These formulas show that either order in each horizontal square gives the common values of Steps 3--5 with $x,b,c$ replaced by $t(x),q^L_{m,n}(b),q^M_{m,n}(c)$. For the unitor use also $t(by)=q^E_{m,n}(b)t(y)$, precisely semilinearity. Apply Step 1 on the sequence site to pass from the section formulas to the map identities. Every sequence-site arrow factors into a horizontal arrow and a vertical arrow by [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], so Steps 6--7 include every restriction. No quotient map has been assumed flat, injective, or split.

source.place: lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product. Agent calculation with the prescribed whole-sequence comparison maps.

proof.text: The equalities above hold for every module system $N$ and are natural in it: the fixed comparisons are natural transformations, and all calculations use their natural units and functor maps. Apply them in each degree of a complex $N^\bullet$. The ordinary inverse-image and tensor functors preserve zero maps (inverse image on abelian sheaves and tensor both send the zero homomorphism to zero), so $F(d^{i+1})F(d^i)=F(0)=0$. For every comparison $a:F\to G$, naturality with the module-system differential $d^i$ is exactly $G(d^i)a_{N^i}=a_{N^{i+1}}F(d^i)$, the cochain-map condition of [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Each equality is degreewise equality of these maps, hence equality of cochain maps. Steps 6--7 apply in every degree as well. No totalization, infinite sum, resolution, or localization occurs, so there is no boundedness restriction.
